Playbook.name: Change Audit — AD Account Lockout (4740) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An account was locked out (4740) - the reshaped, suppressed successor to QA - AD - Account Locked. Triage question: is the lockout the visible symptom of a brute-force/spray, or a benign stale-credential loop (the dominant JCB cause, e.g. achuser locking ~95x/day)?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Lockouts are both a possible brute-force indicator and, in JCB, a major availability drain from stale service-account credentials.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the lockout stems from a credential attack or a benign stale-credential/service loop.

Step.name: Lockout source and recent failures for this account
Step.Purpose: Locate WHERE the bad passwords come from - one device = stale credential; many sources = attack.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4740","4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local/caller") | STATS events = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY src | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One consistent source/caller with steady failures = stale credential (helpdesk fix). Multiple sources or a tight external burst = brute-force. JCB known loop accounts: achuser, aml_srv.

Step.name: Did the account authenticate successfully around the lockout
Step.Purpose: A success from a NEW source near the lockout suggests compromise; success from the normal device = user recovered.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code == "4624" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Success from an unfamiliar source shortly after a lockout is a compromise signal; success only from the user's normal device supports benign recovery.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows failures from multiple/unfamiliar sources, or INV-02 shows success from a new source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Brute-force related lockout - investigate as credential attack)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows one consistent source/caller (stale credential), especially a known loop account (achuser/aml_srv).
A user locked out once from their own device after typos, recovered normally.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-LOCK-SOURCE, INV-02-LOCK-SUCCESS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A user briefly locked out from their own device (typos) and recovered.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm with the user; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: A lockout that is the symptom of a credential attack.

SOCAction.Item: Investigate as brute-force (pivot to PB-AD-002/001); reset if compromise indicators.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A stale stored credential repeatedly locking a service/app account.

SOCAction.Item: Helpdesk: fix the stored credential on the source; track under credential-hygiene P0.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
